name: stays-work
summary: Hosts give guests a bed, and often meals, for their help.
description: Guests help on a farm or in a hostel, with building, or by sitting a house or pets, with no money between them. For adults.

description.description: The stay and the help, in the writer's words: the place, the tasks and the days, and what living there is like.

help.description: What the guest gives for the stay: the help the host asks for, or the guest offers, every kind that applies. Farm work is crops and land; hostel work is reception and helping run a hostel; house-sitting is living in and minding a home while the host is away, with pets or without; teaching is lessons for adults, such as in a language; digital work is photos, social media and websites. A guest's wish for a kind of place, such as a farm, goes in the description.

pets.description: The pets to look after, or that the guest can look after; small pets are such as rabbits or hamsters.

weeklyHours.description: How many hours of help a week: what the host asks, or what the guest gives.

bed.description: Where the guest sleeps: the whole home, as when sitting it, a room of their own, a room shared with others, a caravan or a tent.

hostAway.description: Whether the host is away during the stay, as when the guest sits the house.

meals.description: The meals the host gives the guest each day.

internet.description: Whether the guest has internet at the stay.

welcomes.description: Who the host takes in, for a host who takes only women or only men; left out, anyone.

guests.description: The most guests the host takes at once.

travellers.description: How many people travel together, the guest included.

minNights.description: The fewest nights a guest can stay; a week is 7 nights, a month 30.

nights.description: How many nights the guest wants to stay with one host, within dates; a week is 7 nights, a month 30; left out when dates are the day they arrive and the day they leave.

dates.description: When: in a host's listing, the span the host takes guests in; in a guest's, from the earliest day they could arrive to the latest day they would leave.

languages.description: By ISO 639-1 code, such as en for English: in a host's listing, the languages spoken at the stay, even a little; in a guest's, those the guest can talk in, even a little.

destination.description: Where the guest wants to stay: a circle for each area, such as a town, a region or a country, one for each country of a wider region; a circle may reach past a border.

photos.description: Photos of the place and the help.

asDescribed.description: Whether the stay was as the host's listing said and showed, photos included, the bed, the meals and the help asked: no for any difference the writer names.

helped.description: Whether the guest gave the help agreed.

feltSafe.description: Whether the writer felt safe with them: no if anything made them uneasy; left out when they never met.
